transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Lately I keep having thoughts that my family would be better off if I weren’t here, and it’s starting to scare me. I've just been feeling so completely overwhelmed, and those thoughts made me realize I need to talk to a professional.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or have they been building up more gradually over time?

They really started building up after my father had a stroke about a year and a half ago. Since then, coordinating all of his care on top of my regular job has been dragging me down more and more. It has just been a gradual, heavy pile-up of stress over time that finally brought me to this point.
Over the past month, have you also been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day, or having a lot of worry and tension about many different things that is hard to control?

Yes, absolutely both. I’ve felt this heavy, stuck depression hanging over me almost every minute of the day, and my mind is constantly flooded with uncontrollable worry about my dad’s health, his care costs, and my work. It’s a relentless tension that keeps me awake at night replaying every detail, leaving me completely exhausted.
Have these symptoms been present most days for at least two weeks without a break, or do they mainly come and go only when the stress about your father or work gets worse?

Yes, they are there every single day without any break. This heavy, stuck feeling has been constantly dragging me down ever since my dad's stroke about a year and a half ago. It feels like a permanent cloud over me rather than something that just comes and goes with daily stress.
Before your father’s stroke and the caregiving stress, had you ever had a similar period of depression or constant worry, or is this the first time these symptoms have happened?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before my father's stroke. This is definitely the first time in my life that I’ve felt this way.
Have you had any period of at least two months after your father’s stroke when your mood and worry felt back to normal, or has it stayed nearly constant the whole time?

No, I haven't had any breaks or times where I felt back to normal at all. It has been completely constant and just steadily getting worse ever since his stroke. I haven't felt like my old self for even a week, let alone two months.
When you have thoughts that your family would be better off without you, have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or ending your life, or made any plan to do so?

Yes, especially when I'm driving home late from my parents' place, I catch myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just veered off the road or didn't wake up. It really scares me because I've started picturing how I might actually do it and what things I'd need to get in order first.

Have you ever had a period of at least a few days when you felt unusually energetic or upbeat, needed much less sleep than usual, talked more than normal, or did impulsive things that were out of character?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that; I've never felt unusually energetic, upbeat, or impulsive. Honestly, it has been the exact opposite, where I just feel completely exhausted and drained all the time.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or had changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration?

Yes, I’ve completely lost interest in woodworking and fishing, and my mind is so foggy that I can barely concentrate on blueprints or make decisions. I’m also struggling to sleep more than a few hours a night, I've lost my appetite and weight, and my energy is so low it feels like I'm constantly moving through wet cement.
Did these symptoms begin within a few months of your father’s stroke and caregiving stress, and do they feel directly tied to that stressor rather than happening on their own?

Yes, they definitely started within a few months of his stroke and feel directly tied to that. The overwhelming stress of managing his daily care, the constant decision-making, and losing control over my own life and routine has just dragged me down. It definitely didn't happen on its own; it all stems from that.
Have your symptoms continued for more than 6 months after the stressor began, and do they feel out of proportion to the situation?

Yes, they have been going on for about a year and a half now, which is definitely longer than six months. While the caregiving is incredibly stressful, my reaction feels out of proportion because I feel completely paralyzed and keep thinking my family would be better off without me. It feels like I've completely lost control of how I want to handle things.
Did these symptoms begin only after the caregiving stressor and stay closely tied to it, or did they ever start for no clear reason and persist even when the stress was not present?

They definitely only started after my dad's stroke and the caregiving stress began. I've never had these feelings start for no clear reason, and since the stress has been constant, this heavy feeling has just stayed with me the entire time.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression or loss of interest that started without a major stressor, or has this only happened in response to your father’s stroke and caregiving stress?

No, I have never had an episode like this before; this is the first time in my life I've ever felt this way. These feelings of depression and losing interest only started and built up after my dad's stroke and the caregiving responsibilities began. Before all of this, I was always active with my woodworking, fishing, and chess club, and I never struggled with my mood like this.

Have your symptoms continued even after the caregiving stress eased, or do they improve when the stress is lighter? In other words, do they seem tightly linked to the stressor, or do they feel like a depression that has taken on a life of its own?

The caregiving stress hasn't actually eased at all; it has been constant and ongoing ever since my dad's stroke a year and a half ago. This heavy, stuck feeling has completely taken over my life, so it really does feel like the depression has taken on a life of its own now rather than fluctuating with the daily stress.
Have there been any periods of at least a few weeks when the depression and loss of interest improved a lot, or has it stayed nearly constant even when the caregiving stress briefly felt lighter?

No, there haven't been any periods where it improved; it has just been constant and steadily getting worse ever since my dad's stroke. Even on the rare occasions when the caregiving duties felt a little lighter, this heavy feeling and lack of interest stayed exactly the same. There just hasn't been any break from it at all.

Before your father’s stroke and caregiving stress, had you ever had a similar episode of depression or loss of interest that lasted at least two weeks and happened even when you were not under major stress?
No, I have never experienced anything like this before my father's stroke. This is the very first time in my life that I have felt depressed or lost interest in my hobbies.

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in things even when there was no major stressor, or does it only happen in response to stressful life events?

No, I have never had any periods of feeling depressed or losing interest before this. These feelings only began and have steadily gotten worse since my father's stroke a year and a half ago. Prior to this caregiving stress, I never experienced anything like this at all.

Have you ever had a similar episode of depression or loss of interest that lasted at least two weeks and happened even when you were not under major stress, or does it only happen in response to stressful life events?
No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. It has only happened since my father's stroke and all the stress that followed it.

Have your depression and loss of interest ever continued for at least two weeks even when the caregiving stress was not present or was much lighter, or do they only happen in response to the ongoing stress?

The caregiving stress has been constant and unyielding ever since my father's stroke a year and a half ago, without any break or relief. Because of that, I haven't had a chance to see if the depression and loss of interest would persist without the stress; they have just been continuous and building right alongside the ongoing pressure.
Before your father’s stroke and caregiving stress began, did you ever have a 2-week period of depression or loss of interest that happened even when you were not under major stress?

No, I have never experienced a period of depression or loss of interest like this before my father's stroke. This is completely new territory for me, and it is the first time in my life I've ever felt this way.
Did your depression and loss of interest begin only after your father’s stroke and the caregiving stress, or did they ever start for no clear reason and continue even when the stress was not there?

They definitely only started after my father's stroke and the caregiving stress began about a year and a half ago. It has been a continuous, building struggle tied directly to those ongoing responsibilities. I have never had these feelings start for no clear reason.
Have you had any thoughts of wanting to kill yourself, or made any plan or taken any steps to do so?

Yes, I have. When I'm driving home late from my parents' place, I often catch myself thinking about veering off the road or just wishing I wouldn't wake up the next morning. It really scares me because I've started picturing how I might actually do it and what I would need to get in order first.
Before your father’s stroke and the caregiving stress began, had you ever had a 2-week period of depression or loss of interest that happened even when you were not under major stress?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before my father's stroke. Before that happened, I never had any periods of depression or losing interest in my life. This is the very first time I've ever gone through anything like this.
Have your symptoms ever felt severe enough that they seemed out of proportion to the caregiving stress, or do they mainly track directly with the ongoing stress from your father's illness?

My symptoms definitely track directly with the ongoing stress of caring for my father. It all started building up right after his stroke a year and a half ago, and as the endless caregiving responsibilities became an indefinite, relentless reality, it completely eroded my sense of control and dragged me down to this point.

Have there been any times, even for a few weeks, when your mood and interest improved a lot or felt mostly back to normal, or has the depression stayed present even when the caregiving stress was a little lighter?

No, there haven't been any periods where my mood or interest improved at all. This heavy, stuck feeling has been completely continuous and has steadily dragged me down ever since my dad's stroke a year and a half ago. I haven't had any breaks or times when I felt back to my old self.

Since your father’s stroke, have you ever had a full 2-week period when your mood and interest were back to normal even though the caregiving stress was still there? Or has the depression stayed present most of the time regardless of how the stress was going?

No, I haven't had any breaks or times where I felt back to normal, not even for a week. This heavy, stuck depression has been constant and has steadily dragged me down ever since my dad's stroke a year and a half ago, without any relief at all.
Have you ever had periods of unusual high energy or feeling overly confident, or ever heard or seen things that other people couldn’t?
No, I have never experienced periods of unusually high energy or felt overly confident. I also have never seen or heard things that other people couldn't.
Did your depression and loss of interest start only after your father’s stroke and caregiving stress, or did they ever begin without any clear stressful event?

They definitely only started after my father's stroke and the caregiving stress began about a year and a half ago. I have never experienced these kinds of heavy feelings or lost interest in my life before this stressful period. It all built up gradually as a direct result of trying to manage his care on top of everything else.
If the caregiving stress were to end or become much lighter, do you think your depression and loss of interest would also improve, or would they likely continue even without that stress?

It's really hard for me to even imagine the caregiving stress ending at this point since my dad's situation is so permanent. Because of that, I'm not really sure if things would actually improve, or if this heavy feeling has just become too deeply set to go away on its own.

Have there been any times when you felt noticeably better or more like yourself for at least a couple of weeks, even though your father’s caregiving stress was still going on? Or has the depression stayed present almost all the time no matter what was happening?

No, I haven't had any periods where I felt better or more like myself. This heavy, stuck feeling and depression have been completely constant and dragging me down ever since my father's stroke about a year and a half ago. It just hasn't let up at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with adjustment disorder with depressed mood: symptoms began within months of a major ongoing psychosocial stressor (father’s stroke and caregiving burden), have persisted in close temporal and content-related association with that stressor for about 1.5 years, and include depressed mood, anxiety/worry, insomnia, poor concentration, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, low energy, and suicidal ideation. Although depressive symptoms are prominent, the interview strongly supports a stress-linked adjustment reaction rather than a primary major depressive episode because the onset is clearly tied to the caregiving stressor and the patient repeatedly emphasizes this direct relationship. Major depressive disorder remains a differential because the symptom burden is substantial and persistent.
